transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because the doctor who did my insurance physical said my weight was too low. I don’t really see it that way—I mean, I work painting, I’m up on ladders and moving around all day, so to me I just look lean. But they thought I should get it checked out.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss recently, or has your appetite changed for any reason?

I wouldn’t say it was unintentional exactly. Most days I just keep it pretty light—coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar between jobs, and then a small dinner. A full meal during the day just feels like it would slow me down when I’m working.
Have you ever intentionally tried to keep your weight low or avoid gaining weight, even if it meant eating less than you needed to feel satisfied?

Yeah… I guess so. Like if I go to a client dinner or have bread or something heavier, and the scale is up even a little the next day, I get pretty tense about it. Then I’ll cut back for a day or so because I don’t want it to stick.
After eating something you consider heavy or indulgent, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, or exercise more than usual to avoid gaining weight?
No, I don’t do that. I’ve never made myself throw up or taken laxatives for it. I might just eat lighter afterward, but not those things.
Do you have a strong fear of gaining weight, even if it means going hungry or feeling anxious about what you’ve eaten?
Yeah, I do. If the scale goes up even a little after something like a client dinner or having bread, I get really tense about it. I start cutting back the next day because I don’t want it to stick.
Has your concern about your weight or what you eat ever affected your energy levels, your ability to do your job, or caused any physical symptoms like dizziness or fatigue?

I’m still getting my painting jobs done, so it hasn’t really stopped me from working. But it does affect what I say yes to. I’ll avoid some client meals or social plans because I don’t want it to turn into people watching what I eat or making comments about my weight or how I look.
Do you feel like your body is larger or heavier than it actually is, even when others might not see it that way?

Yeah… I think I do. Like, if I catch myself in a mirror, or I see a photo of me standing next to one of my murals, I’ll zero in on my stomach and my face. If they don’t look sharp enough, it kind of ruins how I feel about myself for the whole day.
How long have you been feeling this way about your weight and eating habits—has this been going on for months, or more like years?
I’m not totally sure how long, honestly. It feels like it’s been a while, but I’d have to think about when it really started. It’s not just a recent week or two, I know that.
Can you estimate how long you’ve been feeling this way about your weight and eating habits—has it been more than six months?
I honestly can’t say for sure. It feels like it could be more than six months, but I don’t want to guess and give you the wrong answer. I know it’s been going on longer than just recently.
Have you been feeling this way about your weight and eating habits consistently, almost every day, for the past six months or more?
I can’t say that confidently. It does feel like it’s been pretty regular, but I haven’t really kept track well enough to say almost every day for six months or more.
Would you say that your concerns about your weight and eating habits have been present for most days over the past six months?
I’m not sure I can say “most days” for sure. I know it’s been on my mind a lot, but I haven’t really been keeping track day by day.
Have you ever felt intense concern about your weight or what you eat, even in situations where it wasn’t really relevant or expected, like during casual meals or events where food wasn’t the focus?

Yeah. Like if I go to a client dinner, or if there’s bread or heavier food around, I’ll be thinking about it more than I probably should. And if the scale is up even a little after that, I get tense and start cutting back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Would you say that your concerns about your weight and eating habits have occurred on most days over the past six months, even if not every single day?
I still don’t really know. It’s been frequent enough that it feels like a pattern, but I can’t honestly say whether it was most days over the whole six months. I just wasn’t tracking it that closely.
Would you say that your concerns about your weight and eating habits have occurred on most days within the past six months, even if not every single day?

I still can’t say for sure that it’s most days. What I can say is, when I have something like a client dinner or eat bread and then the scale is up even a little, I get really tense about it. Then I usually cut back the next day so it doesn’t stay that way.
Would you say that your concerns about your weight and eating habits have occurred on most days within the past six months, even if not every single day?

I can’t say exactly if it’s most days, but it does come up a lot. Like I said, if the scale goes up even a little after a client dinner or after eating bread, I get tense about it and usually cut back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
Would you say that your concerns about your weight and eating habits have occurred on most days within the past six months, even if not every single day?

Yeah, I mean… I’ve said this a few times, but it does happen a lot. If I have a client dinner or eat something with bread and the scale is up even a little, I get tense about it and start cutting back the next day so it doesn’t stay that way.
